title: A highschooler who never coded before made this in an hour. Pretty amazing.
author: Low-Cook-3544

comments.author: lordhiggsboson
comments.body:
What engine are you using?  
The clicking warp effects is pretty neat, is this in-engine effect? Utilizing a shader? Curious to hear about your setup

replies.author: Low-Cook-3544
replies.body: I didn't make it - I hosted a high school hackathon in SF recently where kids made their own games on Rosebud AI. Was honestly surprised with a random high schooler girl coming in late and whipping this up together with a whole other game so I thought I'd share. She generated the assets in Rosebud as well but could obviously take it further with more work using 3D models and stuff. The warping could probably be introduced in the game with a shader but I used screenstudio to record the gameplay which is why you are seeing the effect.

comments.author: Wooden-Hovercraft688
comments.body:
It would be amazing if it wasn't vibe coded.

Not saying the high schooler shouldn't be proud, but it is not really amazing

I'm more proud for LLM's though

comments.author: RemarkableGuidance44
comments.body:
Now can the kid tell you how everything works and can change the code and debug without the LLM?   
  
My 8 year old is making games with the help of AI but I also turn their daily work into a mini course. So they truly understand what is happening. 

This is great but we are getting to the point where anyone can build anything, so the basic game mechanics are just that basic mechanics.

replies.author: Low-Cook-3544
replies.body:
They can definitely see the code changes as they're being implemented. I'd say that if they chose to continue building out the game they could easily learn/understand how the coding bit works. 

I'd push back on the game mechanics being useless - from the 30 high schoolers that attended very few were able to produce something actually playable that also felt this complete. It takes a certain level of attention and creative sense that an 8 year old might have while a 30 year old completely misses. You may not learn to code the hard way but from a broader design thinking perspective it can be so valuable
